matchups.recap:
Paralegal's crew went on a Bust Hike this week, scraping out a 93.0-88.78 win despite a roster that spent most of Sunday bushwhacking without a compass. Josh Jacobs turned in a stunned naval battle queen of a showing at 0.5, Jameson Williams joined him walking on the alpine vegetation at 4.5, and Justin Jefferson's 7.3 means this team got soaking wet at the skill positions. Jonah Coleman carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 16.8, and Travis Kelce chipped in 15.3, which is the only reason Lone Eagle isn't writing an apology letter home.

55 Burgers had every reason to pull this one out and still came up short, Beak as that sounds. Luther Burden III and KC Concepcion both got Guide Recs at 17.2 and 16.8, Trevor Lawrence was steady at 13.58, but D'Andre Swift ate his trail cheese and salami to the tune of 3.1 against a 17.2 projection. Counsel's plan had Boss bones but no legs under it. Sticky buns on Sunday morning go to the Romans, who somehow won the tug of war against their own roster.

Campcraft Enthusiast ran Team Bradford through another session this week and the result was the same tarp-in-a-rainstorm situation we have come to expect. Jordan Love himself posted a Boss 36.18, but the ground crew quit on him entirely — Derrick Henry had his lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow at 5.58 against a projection twice that, DJ Moore managed 5.1, and Jalen Coker turned in 4.6 while Courtland Sutton rotted on the bench scoring nearly triple. Team Bradford is stuck on the Point and Back now, two weeks running, and the plan still looks drawn up with a stick in the dirt.

Old balls, meanwhile, didn't need poetry, just Bucky Irving carrying the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 26.5, Drake Maye chipping in 18.26, and Audric Estime rounding it out at 14.2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had his own quiet afternoon at 8.6, but the margins were there to absorb it, and Funk that Junk went on a Bust Hike to the final bell, winning by 4.9 and banking sticky buns on Sunday Morning for a camp that actually showed up prepared.

Up at the archery range, Ricky Huns banked on Tee Higgins (17.7) and Caleb Williams (12.76) to carry the cabin, and both camper counts came in Boss. But Ladd McConkey took his swing and simply vanished, posting a 0.0 that looked like a Woodsman playing Chief Tyler Hallenbeck in Tetherball — nothing landed, nothing connected, campers just stared. Kyren Williams limped in well under his projection too, and with nearly 21 points stranded on the bench, the whole operation is stuck on the Point and Back, dropping a second straight week despite showing some real flashes.

Harley Jarvis, going by Blue Ridge this week, let Ja'Marr Chase do the carrying like a Woodsman Chief on a hike, dropping 26.5 while Isaiah Likely and the Bears D/ST chipped in tidy, reliable work. The plan wasn't flawless — J.J. McCarthy and Ashton Jeanty both walked on the alpine vegetation, and nearly 40 points sat marooned on the bench — but Blue Ridge still found enough margin to earn a Canoeing Masters finish, 87.18 to 80.86. Sticky buns on Sunday morning for the counselor who adapted just enough; Ricky Huns heads back to the drawing board to find a compass.

The Island Gudge posted the largest margin of victory recorded anywhere this week, a 73.16-point post hike scrub that had every camper at lineup craning their necks. Kenneth Walker III ran like a woodsman running to the camp store on his way to 34.3, Joe Burrow carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 29.54, and Christian Watson chipped in 26.6 of his own. Yes, Quinshon Judkins and Antonio Williams both walked on the alpine vegetation, but when your floor is still this high, nobody's complaining. Had all the arrows in the bullseye this week. I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF.

Catalina Wine Mixon, meanwhile, is stuck on the Point and Back, dropping another one and looking thoroughly Bushwhacking without a compass doing it. Patrick Mahomes and Rhamondre Stevenson did what they could, but Jordan Addison and Adonai Mitchell's matching Dutch Oven-adjacent duds left this roster gonna need to patch those holes with more leaves, because this team got soaking wet. Sixty-six points total — Chief Ron Voice: "I'm disappointed in you."

away.name: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare

matchups.recap:
Flame On rode CeeDee Lamb's 28.5 like a woodsman running to the camp store through the whole week, and even with Ollie Gordon, Devin Singletary, and Jaylen Waddle all walking on the alpine vegetation, Love Thy Naber still ground out a Bust Hike finish worth 106.76. James Cook and Jayden Daniels did their part, which is more than can be said for the three starters who combined to give back nearly 20 projected points. Boss enough to win, Beak enough to make it closer than it should've been.

Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare got Brock Purdy's Boss outing and Christian McCaffrey's usual load, but Tucker Kraft was Stuck in the Sewards all afternoon at 1.4 points, and the Pill Pusher's game plan never found another gear. That's losing streak number two, and this cabin is stuck on the Point and Back with no signs of a real adjustment. Sticky buns and Tuna Casserole head to Love Thy Naber's table this week — the Pill Pusher gets the canoe and the long paddle back to camp.

Chef Boyardee's cabin showed up to the trail with Dak Prescott logging a Boss 19.5 and Brock Bowers chipping in 18.8, but the backfield was Bushwhacking without a compass all afternoon. Jonathan Taylor ate his trail cheese and salami for a measly 6.9 against an 18.25 projection, and Tyler Allgeier limped home at 5.6. Counselor Stefanowitz drew up a plan that looked fine on paper and fell apart the moment the whistle blew, and 90.2 points wasn't going to survive the week against that kind of firepower.

The Machine Knows had its canoe pointed the right way from the first horn, with Puka Nacua going full Pioneer in Gaga ball for 28.0, Matthew Golden matching him at 27.4, and Javonte Williams carrying the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 20.4. Even with Malik Nabers Stuck in the Sewards at 6.8, the Preseason Power Rankings #1 cruised to a well-earned Tuna Casserole and a 120.96 post hike scrub. A 30.76-point margin means this one never saw tug of war — it was target practice.

headline: Week 9 scores are in, mostly as expected
